reference.source: Kanski's Clinical Ophthalmology / Taylor and Hoyt's Pediatric Ophthalmology
clinicalPearls: Coloboma is a gap in one or more ocular structures resulting from failure of the embryonic optic (choroidal) fissure to close, classically located inferonasally
It can affect the iris (producing a keyhole pupil), ciliary body, choroid, retina and optic disc, alone or in combination
Visual impact ranges from minimal, when only the iris is involved, to severe, when the macula or optic nerve is affected
Colobomatous eyes are prone to retinal detachment, so patients should know the warning symptoms
Coloboma is the 'C' of CHARGE syndrome (Coloboma, Heart defects, Atresia of the choanae, Retardation of growth/development, Genital and Ear anomalies), most often caused by CHD7 mutations
Any child with coloboma warrants systemic evaluation for CHARGE and other associations, including hearing assessment
Coloboma also overlaps with the microphthalmia-anophthalmia-coloboma spectrum and may be part of wider syndromes
reference.pathophysiology: Ocular coloboma results from incomplete closure of the optic (choroidal) fissure during early eye development, normally completed in the sixth week of gestation. Persistence of this fissure leaves a defect in the affected layers of the eye, characteristically in the inferonasal quadrant, and the retina and choroid overlying the gap are absent or malformed. In CHARGE syndrome, mutations in the chromatin-remodelling gene CHD7 disrupt development of multiple neural-crest and placode-derived structures during the same embryonic window, so coloboma coexists with cardiac, choanal, growth, genital and ear or hearing anomalies. The malformed retina at the coloboma margin is structurally weak, accounting for the raised risk of retinal detachment.
additionalDifferentials: Microphthalmia and anophthalmia within the same developmental spectrum
Acquired retinochoroidal scarring mimicking a chorioretinal coloboma
Optic disc pit or morning glory disc anomaly
Traumatic or surgical iris defects mimicking iris coloboma
Staphyloma with thinning of ocular coats
Other syndromes featuring coloboma, such as cat-eye syndrome
additionalInvestigations: Dilated fundus examination and slit-lamp assessment to map the extent of coloboma
Ocular imaging including optical coherence tomography and ultrasound to assess involved structures
Systemic evaluation for CHARGE features including cardiac and choanal assessment
Audiological assessment given the frequent ear and hearing involvement
Molecular genetic testing including CHD7 and a broader panel where syndromic
redFlags: Symptoms of retinal detachment such as flashes, floaters or a visual field shadow
Choanal atresia or cardiac anomaly in a neonate with coloboma requiring urgent care
Optic disc or macular involvement threatening central vision
Feeding, breathing or growth difficulties suggesting CHARGE syndrome
reference.prognosis: Visual prognosis depends on which structures are involved, being good for isolated iris coloboma but guarded when the optic nerve, macula or a large chorioretinal area is affected, and further limited by the lifelong risk of retinal detachment; in CHARGE syndrome overall outcome is shaped by the systemic anomalies.
pitfalls: Treating coloboma as purely a cosmetic iris finding and not examining the posterior segment
Failing to evaluate for CHARGE syndrome and associated hearing loss
Overlooking the raised retinal detachment risk and not counselling on warning symptoms
Attributing all visual loss to the coloboma without excluding amblyopia or detachment
references: Taylor and Hoyt's Pediatric Ophthalmology and Strabismus
management: Optical rehabilitation with refractive correction, tinted or contact lenses for iris defects and photophobia, and low-vision aids
Amblyopia treatment in children with refractive correction and occlusion therapy
Lifelong surveillance for retinal detachment with prompt surgical repair, and patient education on warning symptoms
Systemic CHARGE evaluation and management - cardiac assessment, surgical repair of choanal atresia, and feeding and growth support
Audiological assessment with hearing aids or implants for associated hearing loss
CHD7 molecular testing with genetic counselling for the family
Coordinated care through a multidisciplinary team spanning ophthalmology, cardiology, ENT and clinical genetics
